messages.content: Help me create a VMDeathRequest with a suspend policy of EVENT_THREAD and a property 'testProperty' set to 'deathEvent001' in a Java debugging session?

function.name: suspendpolicy017_settingVMDeathRequest
function.description: Creates a VMDeathRequest with the specified suspend policy and property. Throws a JDITestRuntimeException if the request cannot be set. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

suspendPolicy.description: The suspend policy to be used for the VMDeathRequest. This is Java integer type parameter in string representation.

property.description: The property to be associated with the VMDeathRequest. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to create a VMDeathRequest with suspend policy EVENT_THREAD and property 'testProperty' set to 'deathEvent001' in a Java debugging session. We have a tool function: suspendpolicy017_settingVMDeathRequest. It takes suspendPolicy (string) and property (string). We need to call it with suspendPolicy: "EVENT_THREAD" and property: "testProperty=deathEvent001"? Wait property is a string. The description: "The property to be associated with the VMDeathRequest. This is Java String type parameter in string representation." So property likely is a key-value pair? In JDI, VMDeathRequest has a property map? Actually JDI's EventRequestManager has createVMDeathRequest() which returns a VMDeathRequest. The suspend policy is an int: EventRequest.SUSPEND_EVENT_THREAD etc. The property is a string? In JDI, you can set properties on requests via request.setProperty(String key, String value). But the function signature only has property string. Maybe they want to set property key and value as a single string? The function name: suspendpolicy017_settingVMDeathRequest. The description: "Creates a VMDeathRequest with the specified suspend policy and property. Throws a JDITestRuntimeException if the request cannot be set. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax." So we just call the function with suspendPolicy: "EVENT_THREAD" and property: "testProperty=deathEvent001". Or maybe property: "testProperty" and value: "deathEvent001"? But function only has one property param. So likely property string includes both key and value. We'll pass "testProperty=deathEvent001".
